nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا خَلَقْنَاهُمَآ إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
﴿إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾ means: except for the establishing of the truth.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ لاَ يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَن مَّوْلًى شَيْئاً وَلاَ هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ﴾.
al-Mawlā: the ally (al-walī) and the helper, as the poet said:
فَغَدَتْ كِلاَ الفَرْجَيْنِ تَحْسِبُ أنَّهُ * مَوْلَى المَخَافَةِ، خَلْفُهَا وَأَمَامُهَا
(So she set off at dawn, reckoning each of the two openings, behind her and before her, to be the "mawlā" — the place most worthy — of fear.)
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever I am his mawlā, then ʿAlī is his mawlā."
There are three views on its meaning:
The first: that the meaning is: whoever I take as an ally, ʿAlī takes him as an ally.
The second view: whoever takes me as an ally, he [ʿAlī] takes him as an ally.
The third view: it is related that Usāma ibn Zayd said to ʿAlī, peace be upon him: "You are not my mawlā; my mawlā is only the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." So he [the Prophet], peace be upon him, said: "Whoever I am his mawlā, then ʿAlī is his mawlā."

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ شَجَرَةَ ٱلزَّقُّومِ طَعَامُ ٱلأَثِيمِ﴾.
Shuʿba said: I heard Sulaymān [relate] from Mujāhid, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās was sitting with a crook-headed staff (miḥjan) in his hand while the people were circling the House, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O people, fear Allah, and do not die except as Muslims. For if a single drop of al-zaqqūm were to drip upon the people of this world, it would make their livelihood bitter for them — so how about one whose food is al-zaqqūm?"
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: ﴿طَعَامُ ٱلأَثِيمِ﴾: the food of the wicked.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَٱلْمُهْلِ يَغْلِي فِي ٱلْبُطُونِ كَغَلْيِ ٱلْحَمِيمِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Abū Ẓabyān related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-muhl is the dregs of oil.
Then He said ﴿تَغْلِي فِي البُطُونِ﴾, meaning the tree.
And whoever reads ﴿يَغْلِي﴾ makes it refer to the food and al-zaqqūm.
Al-Farrāʾ and Abū Ḥātim said: whoever reads ﴿يَغْلِي﴾ may make it refer to al-muhl.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is an error, because al-muhl is not what boils in the bellies; rather, what boils is only likened to it.
And al-ḥamīm: hot water, as [the poet] said:
* "فِيهَا كِبَاءٌ مُعَدٌّ وَحَمِيمٌ" *
(In it is prepared incense and hot water.)
al-Kibāʾ: incense; one says kabbabtu al-ʿūd, i.e. I burned the aloeswood as incense. And al-kibā, with the short final alif (maqṣūr), is sweepings.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خُذُوهُ فَٱعْتِلُوهُ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ﴾.
That is, He says to the angels: Seize him and drag him.
Mujāhid said: that is, push him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says ʿatalahu, yaʿtuluhu and yaʿtiluhu, when he drags him with violence and force.
Qatāda said: ﴿إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ﴾: to the middle of Hellfire.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْكَرِيمُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, peace be upon them both, read ﴿ذُقْ أنَّكَ﴾ with a fatḥa on the hamza, and it is the reading of al-Kisāʾī. The meaning according to it is: Taste, because you used to say this; and the meaning is: according to your own claim.
Qatāda said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed concerning "Abū Jahl" the verse ﴿أَوْلَى
لَكَ فَأَوْلَى. ثُمَّ أَوْلَى لَكَ فَأَوْلَى﴾, whereupon he said: Does Muḥammad threaten me, when there is none between its two mountains mightier or nobler than I? So Allah revealed ﴿ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْكَرِيمُ﴾, and He revealed concerning him ﴿كَلاَّ لاَ تُطِعْهُ واسْجُدْ وَاقْتَرِبْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ﴾.
Al-Kisāʾī said: al-maqām (with fatḥa) is the place, and al-muqām (with ḍamma) is the residing, as [the poet] said:
* "عَفَتِ الدِّيَارُ مَحَلُّهَا فَمُقَامُهَا" *
(The dwellings have been effaced — their place of halting and their place of staying.)
And the meaning of ﴿أَمِينٍ﴾ is: [secure] from ailments and sorrows.
Qatāda said: "Amīn": [secure] from Satan, from the idol-stones (al-anṣāb), and from sorrows.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَلْبَسُونَ مِن سُندُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ﴾.
ʿIkrima said: al-istabraq is thick brocade.
Abū Isḥāq said: al-istabraq is taken from al-barīq (lustre), and it is what is placed upon the Kaʿba; and al-sundus is the fine [kind] of it.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ وَزَوَّجْنَاهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, We married them [to them].
Qatāda said: and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: ﴿كَذَلِكَ وَزَوَّجْنَاهُمْ بِعِيسٍ
عِينٍ﴾, and its meaning is: the white ones; one says jamal aʿyas (a camel that is aʿyas) when it is white tending towards a reddish-blond tinge.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِكلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ آمِنِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: secure from death, from illness and from Satan.
And someone else said: secure from its being cut off, and from the hidden harm of its ill effects and its unpleasantness; it is not like the fruit of this world, which has hidden harm and runs out.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوْتَةَ ٱلأُولَىٰ وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ﴾.
The meaning is: they will not taste death in it at all. Then He said ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوْتَةَ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾ — an istithnāʾ (exception) that is not from [the genus of] the first [i.e. a disjoined exception]. And Sībawayh recited:
مَنْ كَانَ أَسْرَعَ فِي تَفَرُّقِ فَالجٍ * فَلَبُونُهُ جَرِبَتْ مَعاً وَأَغَدَّتِ
(Whoever was quickest in dispersing [the tribe of] Fālij, may his milch-camels all together become mangy and afflicted with swellings.)
Then he excepted what is not from the first, saying:
إلاَّ كَنَاشِرَةَ التي ضَيَّعْتُمُ * كَالغُصْنِ فِي غُلَوَائِهِ المُتَنَبِّتِ
(Except [one] like Nāshira, whom you neglected, like a branch in the vigour of its sprouting growth.)

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَضْلاً مِّن رَّبِّكَ ذَلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, He did that as a favour.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱرْتَقِبْ إِنَّهُمْ مُّرْتَقِبُونَ﴾.
That is, they are waiting.

nahhas-meani:1-3.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿حمۤ وَٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ﴾ [Verses 1 - 3].
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: ﴿فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ﴾: the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr).
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are three views on the meaning of this verse:
a- Among the soundest of them is what Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The Qurʾān was sent down on the Night of Decree to the lowest heaven
all at once; then Gabriel brought it down over twenty years." This is a chain of transmission that cannot be rejected.
b- And it was said: the meaning is: We sent down a Qurʾān concerning the excellence of the Night of Decree,
namely the saying of the Exalted ﴿لَيْلَةُ القَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ﴾. These are two views.
c- And it was said: the meaning is: We began sending it down on the Night of Decree, as you say: "I
am going out to Mecca tomorrow," i.e. I am beginning the departure.

nahhas-meani:4-5.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ أَمْراً مِّنْ عِنْدِنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ﴾ [Verses 4 and 5].
There are two closely related views on its meaning:
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, settles the affairs of the world until the following year on
the Night of Decree — whatever there is of life, death or provision.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Qatāda said something similar, except that Mujāhid said: except wretchedness and felicity, for these two do not change.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So this is one view.
And the meaning on it is that on the Night of Decree the angels are commanded concerning what there will be of
rain, provision, life and death until the following year.
And the meaning of "yufraqu" and "yuʾmaru" is the same, as though He said: every wise matter is commanded,
as a command from Us.
And the other view: that it is the night of the middle of Shaʿbān, in which the affairs of
the year are settled, the living are copied out from the dead, and the pilgrims are recorded, so that no one is added to them and none is taken away from them.
Someone else said: ﴿يُفْرَقُ﴾: is decreed and set out in detail on that night, until the like of it in the next year.
And ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ means made firm (muḥkam).
And it was said: the meaning of ﴿يُفْرَقُ﴾ is: is separated, i.e. a distinction is made between
the believer, the disbeliever and the hypocrite; this is told to the angels and they know it.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَٱرْتَقِبْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِي ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī ibn
Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, who said: "The sign of the smoke has not yet passed,
and it will come: a smoke will come that afflicts the believers with something like a cold, and the disbeliever will burst."
And al-Aʿmash narrated from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, who said: "A man sat
and said: The smoke has not occurred; it will only be on the Day of Resurrection: something like a cold
will take hold of the believers from it, and it will be severe upon the disbelievers and the hypocrites. So we went in to
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd while he was reclining, and told him what [the man] had said. He got up and sat
angry, and said: When one of you is asked about what he does not know, let him say: I have no knowledge of it; for Allah, Majestic and Mighty, says to His Prophet ﴿قُلْ لاَ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ، ومَا أَنَا مِنَ المُتَكَلِّفِينَ﴾. I will tell you about the smoke: Quraysh rebelled
against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and disbelieved, so he prayed to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, against them that He make them hungry. A severe hunger struck them, until a man would see between the sky and the earth
something like smoke, from hunger and heat. Then Quraysh said ﴿ربَّنَا اكْشِفْ عَنَّا العَذَابُ
إنَّا مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, so Allah removed it from them, and they relapsed; then He seized them with the greatest seizing
on the day of Badr. Had the smoke been on the Day of Resurrection, it would not have been removed from them."

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّا كَاشِفُو ٱلْعَذَابِ قَلِيلاً إِنَّكُمْ عَآئِدُونَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: you will return to sins.
And it is possible that it means: [you will be returning] as dead men.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ ٱلْبَطْشَةَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ إِنَّا مُنتَقِمُونَ﴾.
Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Ibn Masʿūd said about ﴿ٱلْبَطْشَةَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ﴾: it is the day of Badr.
And ʿAwf and Qatāda narrated from al-Ḥasan: ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ ٱلْبَطْشَةَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ﴾: he said: the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَجَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: We tested them.
He said: ﴿وَجَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾: meaning Moses ﷺ.
He said: ﴿وأَنْ لاَ تَعْلُوا عَلَيَّ﴾: that you not be insolent.
He said: And His saying ﴿إنِّي آتِيكُمْ بِسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, that is, with a clear excuse.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ أَن تَرْجُمُونِ﴾.
Qatāda said: with stones.
Al-Farrāʾ said: al-rajm here is killing.
And Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated from Abū Ṣāliḥ concerning ﴿وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ أَن تَرْجُمُونِ﴾: he said: that they should say: a sorcerer, or
a soothsayer, or a poet.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِن لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُواْ لِي فَٱعْتَزِلُونِ﴾.
That is, leave me alone, neither for me nor against me.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱتْرُكِ ٱلْبَحْرَ رَهْواً إِنَّهُمْ جُندٌ مُّغْرَقُونَ﴾.
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿رَهْواً﴾: a road.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: smooth.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿وَٱتْرُكِ ٱلْبَحْرَ رَهْواً﴾:
that is, still; do not command it to return to what it was until the last of them is in it.
And it is narrated from Mujāhid that he said: ﴿رَهْواً﴾: that is, dry.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another. What is still is called
rahw, as the poet said:
والخَيْلُ تَمْرغ رَهْواً فِي أَعِنَّتِهَا * كَالطَّيْرِ يَنْجُو مِنَ الشُّؤْبُوبِ ذِي البَرَدِ
(And the horses move gently (rahwan) in their reins, like birds escaping a hail-laden downpour.)
And it is said: the people came rahwan, in a single ordered line.

nahhas-meani:25-26.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿كَمْ تَرَكُواْ مِن جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ وَزُرُوعٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [Verses 25 and 26].
Al-Farrāʾ said: It is said: the fine dwellings; and it is said: the pulpits.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلأَرْضُ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُنظَرِينَ﴾.
Al-Musayyab ibn Rāfiʿ narrated from ʿAlī, peace be upon him, that he said: "There weep
for the believer the gate through which his deeds ascend, and his place of prayer on earth."
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The believer has a gate
through which his deeds ascend and his provision descends; when he dies, it weeps for him, and
the place where he used to pray weeps for him. But there was no good in the house of Pharaoh, nor did
they have any righteous deed that ascended. Allah the Exalted said ﴿فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلأَرْضُ﴾."
And it was said: the meaning is: the people of the heaven and the people of the earth did not weep for them, as the Exalted said ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: When the Arabs regard someone's death as momentous, they say:
the sky wept for him, and the sun grew dark for him — figuratively — as the poet said:
وَالشَّمْسُ طَالِعَةً لَيْسَتْ بِكَاسِفَةٍ * تَبْكِي عَلَيْكَ نُجُومَ اللَّيلِ وَالقَمَرَا
(The sun, risen yet not eclipsing [them], weeps for you — [alongside] the stars of the night and the moon.)
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا كَانُواْ مُنظَرِينَ﴾: that is, given respite.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَجَّيْنَا بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ مِن فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَالِياً مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: He used to slaughter their sons and spare their women.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَقَدِ ٱخْتَرْنَاهُمْ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عَلَى ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: over the peoples of their own time.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُم مِّنَ ٱلآيَاتِ مَا فِيهِ بَلاَءٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: He saved them from their enemy, brought them across the sea, and sent down
upon them the manna and the quails.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So al-balāʾ here is blessing on this view, as
the poet said:
 * "فَأَبْلاَهُمَا خَيْرَ البَلاَءِ الَّذِي يَبْلُو" *
(And He bestowed on them both the best of the favours with which He tests.)
And al-balāʾ here may be punishment, the opposite of blessing, i.e. affliction overtook them when
they disbelieved in the signs of Allah.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ لَيَقُولُونَ إِنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ مَوْتَتُنَا ٱلأُوْلَىٰ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُنشَرِينَ﴾.
"Inna hāʾulāʾi" means Quraysh; "in hiya" means "mā hiya" (it is not); and al-munsharūn are those resurrected: Allah resurrected (anshara) the dead and they were resurrected (nasharū), as the poet said:
يَا آلَ بَكْرٍ أَنْشِرُوا لِي كُلَيْباً * يَا آلَ بَكْرٍ أَيْنَ أَيْنَ الفِرَارُ؟
(O clan of Bakr, bring Kulayb back to life for me! O clan of Bakr, where, where is the escape?)

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَأْتُواْ بِآبَآئِنَا إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ holds that His saying ﴿فَأْتُواْ﴾ is addressed to the Prophet ﷺ alone,
according to the Arabs' usage in addressing an eminent person.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ﴾.
ʿĀʾisha said: Tubbaʿ was a righteous man; Allah censured his people and did not censure him.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: Ibn ʿAbbās asked Kaʿb: How is it that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, mentioned
the people of Tubbaʿ and did not mention Tubbaʿ? He said: Tubbaʿ was one of the kings, and his people were soothsayers, and with them were some of the People of the Book. His people
used to lie about the People of the Book in his presence, so he said to all of them: Offer a sacrifice. So they offered [sacrifices],
and the sacrifice of the People of the Book was accepted while the sacrifice of his people was not accepted, so he embraced Islam. For that reason
Allah mentioned his people and did not mention him.
